cls: Antiarrhythmic - Class IC (sodium channel blocker) with beta-blocking activity
quick: IR: 150 mg every 8 h; may titrate to 300 mg every 8 h
May take with or without food; be consistent
Limited data; use only if benefit outweighs risk
Excreted in milk; use with caution
ECG/QRS, heart rate, proarrhythmia, BP, signs of CHF
summary: Propafenone is a Class IC antiarrhythmic that slows cardiac conduction by blocking fast sodium channels and also has weak beta-adrenergic blocking activity. It is used to maintain sinus rhythm in symptomatic atrial fibrillation and to treat life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias and PSVT. Because of proarrhythmic risk (notably the CAST experience with Class IC drugs), it must be avoided in structural heart disease and started with ECG monitoring.
indications: Prolong the time to recurrence of symptomatic atrial fibrillation in patients without structural heart disease
Treatment of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT) associated with disabling symptoms
Treatment of documented life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias such as sustained ventricular tachycardia

dosage.d: Increase to 225 mg then up to 300 mg every 8 hours
225 mg every 12 hours; titrate to 325 mg then 425 mg every 12 h
Single oral dose ~450-600 mg by weight (specialist directed)

admin: Initiate in a monitored setting given proarrhythmic risk
Swallow extended-release capsules whole; do not crush or chew
Take at consistent times relative to food
Obtain a baseline ECG; recheck QRS duration and rhythm after dose changes
Often combined with an AV-nodal blocker in atrial fibrillation to prevent rapid 1:1 conduction of atrial flutter
moa: Propafenone blocks fast inward sodium channels (Class IC), markedly slowing the rate of rise of the cardiac action potential and reducing conduction velocity in atrial, AV-nodal, His-Purkinje and ventricular tissue. It also has weak (non-selective) beta-adrenergic blocking activity and mild calcium-channel blocking effects, prolonging the PR interval and QRS duration.

absolute: Heart failure / significant structural heart disease
Sinoatrial, AV and intraventricular conduction disorders or sick sinus syndrome without a pacemaker
Bronchospastic disorders / severe COPD or asthma (beta-blocking effect)
monitor: Signs of heart failure and proarrhythmia

preg: Limited human data; crosses the placenta. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Propafenone is excreted into breast milk. Use with caution during breastfeeding and monitor the infant.
renal: Metabolites are renally excreted and can accumulate; use with caution in renal impairment and monitor closely, as the contribution of metabolites to efficacy and toxicity is not fully defined.
hepatic: Hepatic metabolism is the main clearance route; clearance is markedly reduced in hepatic impairment. Reduce the dose substantially and monitor closely.

major: CYP2D6 inhibitors (quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine) - raise propafenone levels
CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, ritonavir) combined with CYP2D6 inhibition - markedly raise levels
Other antiarrhythmics and QRS/QT-prolonging drugs - additive proarrhythmia
moderate: Beta-blockers - additive negative chronotropy/inotropy and increased beta-blocker levels
Rifampin (CYP inducer) - reduced propafenone levels and efficacy
minor: Local anesthetics - additive CNS adverse effects
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; take consistently.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; it may worsen arrhythmia and additive CNS effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Widens QRS and prolongs PR on ECG; may elevate ANA titers and rarely cause positive ANA.

serious: Proarrhythmia - new or worsened ventricular arrhythmia (including torsades), atrial flutter with rapid 1:1 AV conduction
Severe bradycardia / AV block / sinus arrest

monitoring: Baseline and periodic ECG (QRS, PR, QT) and rhythm
Signs/symptoms of heart failure and proarrhythmia
Serum electrolytes; correct before and during therapy
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed and do not stop abruptly without advice
Report palpitations, fainting, chest pain, severe dizziness or worsening breathlessness immediately
A bitter or metallic taste is common
Tell your doctor about all other medicines, especially other heart-rhythm drugs, antidepressants and warfarin
Report fever, sore throat or signs of infection (possible low white cells)
pk: Antiarrhythmic effect within hours of an oral dose
Extensive metabolizers ~2-10 h; poor metabolizers ~10-32 h
IR dosed every 8 h; ER every 12 h owing to saturable metabolism
Store at controlled room temperature, protected from moisture
pearls: AVOID in structural heart disease/heart failure - Class IC drugs increased mortality post-MI (CAST trial); proarrhythmia is the key danger
Has intrinsic weak beta-blocking activity - can worsen asthma/COPD and cause bradycardia
In atrial fibrillation/flutter, co-prescribe an AV-nodal blocker to prevent dangerous 1:1 conduction if atrial flutter develops
CYP2D6 polymorphism: poor metabolizers have higher levels and more beta-blockade
QRS widening >25% from baseline signals excessive effect - reduce dose
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is close to the next scheduled dose, skip it and resume the usual schedule. Never take two doses at once.
overdose: Overdose causes hypotension, bradycardia, conduction block, wide QRS, ventricular arrhythmias, seizures and high-degree AV block. Management is supportive: cardiac monitoring, sodium bicarbonate for wide-QRS sodium-channel toxicity, vasopressors/atropine, temporary pacing and seizure control. Not effectively dialyzed.
